participants: Andrew Jin / Andrew Musial (closer, Primal Instinct)
summary: Monday sales team meeting: wins round, weekly projections and a partial call review. Chris coaches the closers on finding a gap big enough that the prospect would pay $6,000 to solve it, and on driving goals from surface to action to identity level so the $6,000 objection never becomes a value objection. Andrew reports three units and $7,200 cash for the prior week against target, and explains he closed one uncertain prospect on a 'love it or leave it' arrangement rather than the six-month programme. Ben, newly ramping, reports one unit and a first PIF. Setter numbers are reviewed (Kim 20 sets at 79.6% show, Kyla six units) and Kim is asked to run a breakout coaching session for Kyla. The last twenty minutes are a review of Andrew's call with 'Manny', a Blue Origin technical project manager and Air Force reservist with a pre-diabetes diagnosis and a family history of diabetes, cancer and high cholesterol; Chris cuts the review short for a landlord call.
notable: Chris confirms a CRM policy: every booked sales call must have a custom activity logged in Close - completed, not completed, no-show or rescheduled - 'for every single person that's on your calendar, ever'. This is the mechanism by which the corpus denominator is built.

A 'love it or leave it' arrangement is in active use as a fallback for uncertain prospects. Chris permits it but sets a boundary: 'that's where I start to, like, kind of draw the line with the love it or leave it if we're just offering it to everybody.'

Chris coaches the team to project absolute certainty of results - 'have full conviction that we get results and it's science... If they eat the foods and they do the work, the result has to happen. It's human biology has to happen.' This is the origin of the unbounded guarantees that appear later in the batch on live calls.
Third-party financing is referred to as 'Paiva' and Ben notes it 'only goes up to 12 months'.
Vegetarian prospects are a recurring objection against Trevor's meat-based nutrition; Chris's answer is 'there's ways around it' with no documented protocol.
Two reps ridicule a prospect's sexual orientation at length after learning he has a boyfriend, on the recorded call. Flagged separately.
Prospects are characterised by ethnicity in the course of coaching - 'so freaking Silicon Valley engineer, analytical Indian guy'. Flagged separately.

Rep name discrepancy across the whole folder: every transcript labels the closer 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' while the batch folder and all call titles name him Andrew Musial. Same person - Poland-based closer - but rep-level rollups keyed on the speaker label will not join.
